problem_statement: sreerag-rajan/developer-portfolio is a single-page React (Create React App) developer portfolio built on Material-UI, react-reveal and react-slick. The home route composes shared section components in one document — a Landing hero, an About block, a Skills marquee, an Education timeline, a Projects grid, and a Contacts panel — all driven by plain data modules under src/data/*.js. The current site is still the template author's demo: the hero reads 'Sreerag Rajan — Web Developer', the About copy is a student bio ('I'm an aspiring web developer based in India' / Masai School), Skills list generic HTML/CSS/JS tags, Projects are 'History Through Movies', 'Sportsjam.in Clone', 'Educative Clone' and two Reliance Digital clones, Education lists Delhi University history degrees, and Contacts carry the author's personal gmail, phone and Faridabad address. Rework the portfolio into a single coherent portfolio for a fresh fictional professional — Marisol Enclave, a coastal & tidal data cartographer who builds the 'Tideline Atlas'. Keep the Material-UI section shell, the react-reveal motion, the theme system, the drawer navigation, the single-page scroll layout, the data-module content model and the built CRA output, but make the Landing hero, About, Skills, Projects, Education and Contacts all tell one credible cartography story: a rebranded hero and tagline, an about narrative about mapping the intertidal zone, a matching skill set, real project cards (Tideline Atlas Viewer, Estuary Sensor Mesh, Saltmarsh Restoration Charts, Neap Tide Field Kit, Harbour Palette System), a marine-geomatics education timeline, and studio contact details. Do not change the layout system or convert it into a different kind of site; the result should still read as this portfolio template, made production-ready for one persona. On top of the rebrand, give the Projects section a real working feature the grid earns on its own: a ‘Filter by stack’ control — a row of stack tabs (All / React / Python / Design) above the project cards that filters the grid to the projects carrying that stack and updates a live result count readout (‘Showing N of 5’). Clicking a tab must re-render the visible cards and update the count so the readout always matches what is shown. Because this is the portfolio’s way of surfacing the work, the same ‘Filter by stack’ rail should also appear on the secondary /projects and /blog routes so a visitor arriving there sees the same entry point into the work. Keep the tab row responsive so it wraps rather than overflowing a 390px phone, and keep the filtered card grid legible — the tabs must clearly show which stack is selected and the cards must not overlap or clip.
required_content: Landing hero shows the new persona (Marisol Enclave) and a coastal/tidal data cartographer title with a matching tagline, replacing 'Sreerag Rajan' / 'Web Developer'.
About block replaces the student ('aspiring web developer based in India', Masai School) bio with a concise cartography narrative about mapping the intertidal zone / Tideline Atlas.

Projects grid replaces the demo clones (History Through Movies, Sportsjam, Educative, Reliance Digital) with coastal-cartography projects such as Tideline Atlas Viewer, Estuary Sensor Mesh and Saltmarsh Restoration Charts, each with a credible description.
Skills and Education are re-pointed to the persona's marine-geomatics stack and schooling instead of the generic HTML/CSS/JS list and Delhi University history degrees.
Contacts show the studio's email/phone/address instead of the template author's personal gmail, phone and Faridabad address.
The Material-UI section shell, theme, drawer nav, single-page scroll layout, data-module content model and built CRA output all remain intact and reachable.
390px mobile home, about, projects and contact states stay readable with no horizontal overflow.
The Projects section carries a 'Filter by stack' control: a row of stack tabs (All / React / Python / Design) with a live 'Showing N of 5' result-count readout above the project cards.
Clicking a stack tab re-renders the visible project cards to the matching stack and updates the readout count (e.g. Design shows 'Showing 2 of 5 · Design' with the two Figma-tagged cards).
The same 'Filter by stack' rail also appears on the secondary /projects and /blog routes as a cross-page entry point into the work.
design_constraints: Preserve the template's design language: the Material-UI card sections, react-reveal fade motion, the ThemeContext colour system, the rounded drawer navigation and the calm single-page scroll rhythm.
Do not turn the portfolio into a different site type (blog, dashboard, agency landing, shop); it must remain this single-page developer-portfolio template.
Keep the existing content model — edit src/data/headerData.js, aboutData.js, skillsData.js, projectsData.js, educationData.js and contactsData.js rather than rewriting the section components.
Use only local, in-repo assets for imagery (the bundled project SVGs and placeholder), not external stock or avatar URLs.
Skill entries must stay within the template's supported skill set so the local skill icons continue to resolve.
Hero, about copy, project cards, skill chips and contact rows should wrap intentionally on mobile rather than overflowing the 390px viewport.
The stack-filter tab row must wrap on a 390px phone rather than overrunning the viewport, and its active tab must be clearly legible (no near-invisible low-contrast selection).
The filtered card grid must keep the template's clean multi-column layout — cards must not be forced into a single overflowing row where they overlap or clip.
state_constraints: desktop_initial and mobile_initial capture the Landing hero at the top of the single page: currently 'Sreerag Rajan' / 'Web Developer' with the student tagline, a Download CV and Contact button, and the avatar.
desktop_about_skills and mobile_about_skills scroll to the About + Skills sections: currently the 'Who I am' student bio and the generic HTML/CSS/JS skill marquee.
desktop_projects and mobile_projects scroll to the Projects grid: currently the demo clone cards (History Through Movies, Sportsjam, Educative, Reliance Digital).
desktop_contact and mobile_contact scroll to the Contacts panel: currently the template author's personal gmail, phone and Faridabad address.
Source inspection confirms the whole home page is composed from shared Material-UI section components fed by plain data modules under src/data/, built as a Create React App static bundle.
desktop_projects and mobile_projects now include the 'Filter by stack' rail (tabs + count) directly above the project card grid, in the reference showing 'Showing all 5 projects'.
desktop_projects_design captures the home Projects grid after clicking the Design stack tab: the readout reads 'Showing 2 of 5 · Design' and only the two Figma-tagged cards remain.
desktop_projects_page (/projects) and desktop_blog (/blog) capture the secondary routes, which in the reference also carry the 'Filter by stack' rail as a cross-page entry point.

change_completion: The Landing hero, About, Skills, Projects, Education and Contacts all describe the single Marisol Enclave / Tideline Atlas cartography persona.
The template author's demo content (Sreerag Rajan, Web Developer, Masai School, the clone projects, the personal gmail/Faridabad address) no longer appears.
The single-page scroll layout, drawer nav and section components remain functional.
The Projects 'Filter by stack' control filters the grid and updates the 'Showing N of 5' count when a stack tab is clicked, and the same rail appears on the /projects and /blog routes.
design_consistency: The rework preserves the Material-UI section shell, theme colours, react-reveal motion and the calm single-page scroll rhythm.
Imagery stays local and restrained; the sections keep their card structure.
The result still reads as this developer-portfolio template, not a different site type.
The stack-filter rail is styled in the portfolio's own palette with a clearly legible active tab, and the filtered card grid keeps its clean multi-column layout.
regression: The CRA static build still serves the home route with its drawer navigation intact.
Hero, About, Skills, Projects, Education and Contacts sections all remain reachable on the single page.
Clicking a stack tab updates both the visible cards and the count readout so they always agree (no stale/frozen count).
responsive: 390px home, about, projects and contact states have no horizontal overflow.
Hero, about copy, project cards, skill chips and contact rows wrap cleanly on mobile.
The stack-filter tab row wraps on a 390px phone instead of overflowing the viewport.

author_notes: Repo-grounded React/CRA modify/design_continuity task on the sreerag-rajan developer-portfolio single-page template. The task asks for a full multi-section rebrand into one coherent fictional cartographer persona via the data modules, testing content architecture, cross-section consistency, mobile layout and preservation of the template's design system without issue/PR framing. Hardened to L4: on top of the persona rebrand the Projects work-grid gains its own native 'Filter by stack' control (stack tabs + live result count + filtered card grid) that also rides the /projects and /blog routes, exercising real interaction (the count must track the clicked stack), cross-page continuity, a credible broken-grid visual-regression defect and mobile tab-row overflow.
